note: A local Anvil fork of HSK mainnet. Hashes exist only on the fork. Nothing was broadcast to any public network.

steps.name: preflight: chain, code, factory, tokens, fee and oracle all check out
deploy
limits, conditional on what was read: 10 HSK a trade, 20 an hour, 40 a day, 60 ever, floor 0.05
the daily budget
a guardian, which can stop things and nothing else
the price guard: within 100 ticks of a 600 s TWAP
fund the vault with 300 WHSK
simulate mode: the vault's real answer, by eth_call, with no key loaded and no funds moved
live: a market sell through the real router, preflighted, whose calldata carries its decision's hash
attack: with the pool really pushed, the agent holds twice over and sends nothing

detail.ownCheck: Market order into-push: spot is 1165 bps from TWAP, over 200.
detail.vaultBand: Order into-push: this trade would leave the pool 1163 ticks from its TWAP, past the vault's band of 100.

steps.name: attack: a thief with the agent key skips the agent and goes straight to the vault, which refuses on chain
attack: the agent key cannot withdraw
arm the stop: 200 ticks down, 10 HSK a tranche, 30 in all, floor 0.03
the keeper waits: one real push crossed the trigger at spot, and not on the TWAP
the keeper's dry run reports what it would do, and moves nothing
the keeper refuses to send on chain 177 without --confirm-mainnet
after the price held for the window, a stranger's key fired the stop and the vault kept the proceeds
the stop then waits out its cooldown
rotate the agent key
the old agent key no longer does anything, not even pause
the guardian ends the agent key
the guardian halts: trading and the stop both end
the guardian can neither take funds nor restart anything
the owner withdraws everything, from a halted vault with a revoked key
the monitor reports the revoked key as critical, and exits 2

steps.name: measured what it costs to push this pool

manipulationCost.method: Sell into the real pool on a fork and buy straight back, with no other trader acting. This is the floor on the cost: holding a price for a whole TWAP window adds arbitrage losses, which a fork with no other traders cannot measure.
